author: Shireen Gandhi, Temporary Commissioner
title: Corrective Action Plan for Program Integrity (original, to CMS)
notes: Addressed to Kim Brandt (CMS Chief Operating Officer and Deputy Administrator) and Daniel Brillman (Deputy Administrator). Closes the 'first CAP PDF not fetched' gap in research/harvest/oversight-law/GAPS.md item 2.
supports: DHS states this CAP is submitted 'in response to your letter of December 5, 2025, in which you requested a plan from Minnesota to strengthen program integrity and anti-fraud actions within its Medicaid program' -- primary-source confirmation of the existence, approximate subject, and exact date of the CMS letter that GAPS.md previously listed only as 'cited in the 30 Jan CAP,' not itself fetched.

DHS states 'as we stated in our December 17 reply to your letter, we strongly agree that assertive, ongoing action is necessary' -- this discloses a previously-unknown DHS-to-CMS communication dated December 17, 2025, an interim reply between the December 5 CMS letter and this December 31 CAP. Not previously known to this corpus.
Governor Walz issued Executive Order 25-10 on September 17, 2025 to bolster and expand Medicaid program-integrity work.
DHS states it designated EIDBI and Housing Stabilization Services (HSS) as high-risk 'early in 2025,' providing additional program-integrity tools including unannounced on-site visits.
DHS states it requested CMS assistance on August 1, 2025 to terminate the HSS benefit, and that CMS approved shuttering the HSS program 'at the end of October' 2025.
DHS states it disenrolled 'over 800 inactive providers in October 2025 alone,' following a CMS suggestion made during HSS termination discussions.
does_not_support: The text of the December 5, 2025 CMS letter itself, or the December 17, 2025 DHS reply -- both are referenced here but not attached or quoted at length, and neither has been independently retrieved.

Any claim about what specific program-integrity actions the December 5 CMS letter demanded beyond 'strengthen program integrity and anti-fraud actions'; that characterization is DHS's own summary of CMS's letter, not a direct quotation of it.
